daily_reality.typical_workday: Average 42-44 hours/week, significantly lower than most medical specialties. Typical 8AM-5PM, four days/week for patient care. See 15-22 patients/day in outpatient settings. Day starts with answering patient cases (30 min), then physical exams, diagnostic tests (skin prick, intradermal, patch tests), prescribing medications, developing treatment plans. Lunch break for charting, calls, staff meetings. End day with charting and emails. Fridays often reserved for admin work, accounting, and CME. No or minimal overnight call. Very few inpatient responsibilities.

daily_reality.seasonality: Spring and fall allergy seasons (tree pollen March-May, ragweed August-October) create peak patient volumes. Asthma exacerbations increase in fall/winter. Food allergy consultations spike around holidays. Immunotherapy start-ups often clustered in winter. Year-round demand for immunodeficiency patients.

laws: FDA regulations on allergen extracts and biologics
regulatory.licensing: MD or DO degree. Board certification in Internal Medicine (ABIM) or Pediatrics (ABP) first. 24+ months allergy/immunology fellowship (ACGME-accredited). ABAI Certification Examination ($2,650). 5-year window for certification after fellowship. MOC: 10-year cycles, 25 CME credits annually, Continuous Qualification Examination. DEA registration required.
regulatory.penalties: License revocation/suspension disqualifies from certification. Restricted licenses affect MOC status. MIPS non-compliance: negative payment adjustments. Solo practitioners face highest penalty rates (49.16%). Malpractice liability for anaphylaxis management errors. Exam misconduct: civil/criminal liability. CQE annual fee: $2,500; CCP annual fee: $400.

career_psychology.burnout: 35-39% burnout rate (lower than 45-54% national physician average). Top causes: bureaucratic tasks (52%), EHR burden (25-40% excessive home EMR time), inadequate compensation (32%), decreasing reimbursements (28%). 50% report great deal of job stress. 60% say burnout affects personal relationships. Coping: 51% talk with family/friends, 39% exercise, 39% sleep. Private practice has less burnout than hospital employment. 50% would take salary reduction for better work-life balance.
